old: # The conditions prior
new: # The conditions prior

old: Where there is science and a method for problems, five conditions hold before the method acts.
new: Where science has a method for problems, five conditions stand prior to its acting.
why: hold: stand; the method: its, a method for problems and not the one method.

old:
The statement holds across readings.

The terms have determinate reference.

The accounts hold their truth value while tested.

A procedure repeated returns the same outcome independently of what precedes it.

Nothing prior enters: what comes to the statement carries nothing of what it carried before.
new:
The statement holds across readings.

The terms have determinate reference.

The accounts hold their truth value while tested.

A procedure repeated returns the same outcome independently of what precedes it.

Nothing prior enters: what comes to the statement carries nothing of what it carried before.
why: scientific method's five conditions in its own terms (holds across readings, truth value, determinate reference, replication); each entry of part 5 repeats them word for word and check C5 tests entries against them as they stand, so re-saying them here would part the front from 255 kept entries.

old: The first is required by replication, the second by measurement, the third by inference, the fourth by replication.
new: The first is required by replication, the second by measurement, the third by inference, the fourth by replication.
why: the kept: an only first, second, third and fourth within its own set of five; replication, measurement and inference a field's own terms.

old: The fifth is a condition on what reaches a statement, and the first four stand on it: a statement holds across readings where nothing arriving at it brings a prior reading.
new: The fifth is a condition on what reaches a statement, and the first four stand on it: a statement stands across readings where nothing arriving to it brings a prior reading.
why: hold: stands; at: to; the fifth and the first four kept, only within their set of five.

old: A problem adds a sixth, its own, fixing what comes out: its outcome preserves a stated relation over a stated range.
new: A problem adds a sixth, its own, fixing its outcome: its outcome preserves a stated relation over a stated range.
why: out: re-said by meaning, what comes out is its outcome.

old: This condition is a problem's and not a method's, and it stands at Conserving relation and Conserving reach in every entry.
new: This condition is a problem's and not a method's, and it stands with Conserving relation and Conserving reach of every entry.

old: This is an open registry: a set of entries on a stated population, each carrying the same properties.
new: This is an open registry: a set of entries over a stated set of problems, each carrying one same set of properties.
why: statistics: a population re-said as a stated set of problems; the: one same set.

old: **The problems stand open.**
new: **Problems stand open.**

old: No entry carries a settled answer to its own statement, except where its record settles one and the entry carries that settling.
new: No entry carries a settled answer to its own statement, except where its record settles one and its entry carries that settling.

old: **The intake stands open.**
new: **Intake stands open.**

old: An arrival is entered, and the collection is added to as arrivals come.
new: An arrival is entered, and this registry's collection is added to as arrivals come.

old: **The properties and checks stand open.**
new: **Properties and checks stand open.**

old: Every property is stated at section 4 and every check at section 6.
new: Every property stands stated with section 4, and every check with section 6.

old: Any of them is executed against fields' literature, by anyone holding it.
new: Any of them is executed against fields' literature, by anyone with that literature.

old: **Every line stands open at an address.**
new: **Every line stands open with an address.**

old: A line without an address makes a claim nothing reaches, and check C1 tests for it.
new: A line without an address is a claim nothing reaches, and it is check C1's case.

old: Every entry carries the same properties, in the same order, whatever its field.
new: Every entry carries one same set of properties, with one same order, whatever its field.

old: Its schema is closed once, at one place, so that nothing else has to be.
new: Its schema is closed once, one place only, so that nothing else has to be.

old: # 2 Hard problems in science
new: # 2 Hard problems in science

old: **Problems in science** are hypotheses.
new: **Science's problems** are hypotheses.
why: in: re-said by meaning, problems of science.

old: Where a consequence is borne out, nothing follows about its account, a rival account entailing the same consequence.
new: Where a consequence is found true, nothing follows about its account, a rival account entailing that same consequence.
why: out: borne out re-said by meaning, found true; the: that.

old: **Hard** is where testing continues and returns no refutation: either no consequence separating accounts is derivable, or accounts entail the same consequences.
new: **Hard** is where testing continues and returns no refutation: either no consequence separating accounts is derivable, or accounts entail one same set of consequences.
why: the: one same set; hardness a property of a hypothesis with what it carries, not a possibly existing thing.

old: **Progress** is what stands: established, measured, proved, or ruled out.
new: **Progress** is what stands: established, measured, proved, or excluded.
why: out: ruled out re-said as excluded, as 4.3's register says it.

old: It accumulates whether or not a problem settles, every approach that ends returning a result about the approach.
new: It accumulates whether or not a problem settles, every approach that ends returning a result about itself.

old: Each entry states one problem as it is posed, and carries progress and persistence with a remainder between them visible.
new: Each entry is one problem's statement as it is posed, carrying progress and persistence with a remainder between them visible.
why: doer: an entry stating becomes the entry as a statement; a registry records.

old: Every entry carries the same properties, filled from a record at which each is verified.
new: Every entry carries one same set of properties, filled from a record by which each is verified.
why: the: one same set; at: by.

old: A test therefore returns no indication of which specification is at issue where a settling result requires one to fall.
new: A test therefore returns no indication of which specification falls, where a settling result requires one to fall.

old: A specification is universal under a name where it is fixed across everything stated under that name, and local where it is fixed at one statement.
new: A specification is universal under a name where it is fixed across everything stated under that name, and local where it is fixed to one statement.

old: No specification is identified as the one to withdraw, and specifications stand at the number brought in.
new: No specification is identified as one to withdraw, and specifications stand as many as were brought.
why: the: removed; at, in: re-said by meaning.

old: A result is replicated where the same procedure returns the same outcome independently of what precedes it.
new: A result is replicated where one same procedure returns one same outcome independently of what precedes it.

old: Accumulation stands in specifications.
new: Accumulation stands as specifications.
why: in: as, by meaning; what accumulates is specifications.

old: Inference reads specifications at the start of a test and writes to them at no point.
new: Inference reads specifications as a test opens and writes to none of them.
why: at, the: re-said by meaning; inference reading and writing kept as the field's own account of its method.

old: The number of hypotheses tested measures testing.
new: Testing is measured by its count of hypotheses tested.
why: the: its; a count is a measure here, not a likelihood.

new: ## 4.1 The properties

new: Their number stands against a count of consequences derivable.

old: What the statement quantifies over.
new: What a statement quantifies over.

new: Where a relation between these two is stated — an equivalence, a proved limitation, an account of what a method does not deliver — that statement stands.

old: What was attempted stands at Approaches.
new: What was attempted stands with Approaches.
